tools.name: framefetch_platform_capabilities
tools.description: JSON matrix of data types (metadata, insights, transcript, frames, comments) per platform — YouTube (+Shorts), TikTok, Instagram Reels, Pinterest, Reddit. Call before framefetch_extract to confirm support. No input.

tools.name: framefetch_search
tools.description: Search YouTube by keyword (yt-dlp, no login). Returns up to `limit` hits: url/title/uploader/durationSec/uploadDate(often null)/thumbnail/views. YouTube only — use framefetch_extract on a hit's url for transcript/frames/etc. Billed ~$0.002/call (metadata-tier), regardless of `limit`.

tools.description: Check this account's credit balance/usage. Read-only — never charges; works at zero balance (unlike framefetch_extract). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: framefetch_search, framefetch_account · Private data: framefetch_extract · Public sink: framefetch_extract, framefetch_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: framefetch_search, framefetch_account · Private data: framefetch_extract · Public sink: framefetch_extract, framefetch_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
